v1.feedback: The Boltanski shadow-projection concept is a genuine morphological addition to the parent tower — umbra reads as eclipse, not just dimming. The penumbral amber edge glow (0x9a7a50) is well-restrained but could be more spatially directional: tie it to actual light-to-surface angle rather than a periodic absence function so the penumbra boundary feels physically motivated. The shadow-wall particles risk reading as a second disconnected cloud; tighten the projection geometry so every shadow particle traces a clear ray from the point light through the tower silhouette — that hard geometric relationship is what makes Boltanski installations legible in 2 seconds.

v2.feedback: The shadow-projection concept is a genuine morph — inherited tower darkened with ray-cast shadow doubles on a ground plane is conceptually strong and reads as the parent transformed by 'umbra'. However, the tower palette (0x5a5550 / 0x3d3a36) against a 0x0a0908 background may collapse into murk, making the tower itself hard to read in 2s; bump the tower base color up a stop or add a subtle rim highlight so the silhouette separates from the void. The shadow particles use random scatter offsets that risk reading as a noise blob rather than a crisp projected silhouette — tighten the displacement or weight it by distance-from-light-axis so the shadow sharpens near center and only softens at penumbral edges. The amber edge color (0x9a7a50) is the most alive element; let it do more work on the tower side too, not just as a subtle 0.6-mix bleed.
